documents.title: Cough / weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Cough about 3 weeks, mostly dry, some days a little clear phlegm, not getting better. No fever, no blood. Not short of breath on the job. Clothes looser - he weighed 89 at endo in the fall, 84 today, not trying. Appetite "meh".
Also: saw nephrology for the first time in January. Per pt they said kidney function is reduced but stable and to keep his medicines as they are and return in the fall. No letter here yet. Laser to both eyes done Dec and Jan, letter received.

O: Afebrile, sat as charted. Diminished breath sounds at the right base, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No nodes in neck or supraclavicular area. Trace ankle edema, same as fall.
CXR (in-house read): mass-like opacity right lower lobe.

A/P
- RLL opacity with cough and 5 kg unintended loss in a 30 pack-year former smoker. Concerned for malignancy. CT chest with contrast ordered urgently; BMP today to confirm kidney function is ok for contrast, hydrate. Called pt with the x-ray result before he left.
- Requested January nephrology note.
Will call with CT.

reports.text:
CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison: chest radiograph 02/07/2024 and low-dose CT 12/08/2020.
Lungs: A 4.0 cm solid mass in the right lower lobe, new since 2020. No other pulmonary nodules. No consolidation.
Mediastinum: Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes in the right paratracheal, subcarinal and left paratracheal stations. Heart normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
Pleura: No effusion.
Upper abdomen: Adrenal glands and liver unremarkable on the included images.
Bones: No suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right lower lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy, highly suspicious for primary lung cancer. Tissue sampling and PET-CT staging recommended.

orders.order: MRI brain with and without contrast

orders.reason: suspected lung cancer with mediastinal nodes

documents.title: CT result discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mark (wife on speaker) at 7 before his shift. Went over the CT: 4 cm mass in the lower right lung and enlarged lymph nodes in the middle of the chest; most likely a lung cancer, needs a biopsy to know for sure and what kind. He was quiet, then asked if it had spread. Told him the nodes in the chest are involved, we need a PET scan and brain MRI to see the rest. Orders in for PET-CT and MRI brain, referrals to thoracic surgery (for biopsy of the nodes) and oncology, both marked urgent. He can call or text me anytime. Will check in after biopsy.

reports.text:
FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh. Fasting glucose acceptable for imaging.
Chest: Intensely FDG-avid right lower lobe mass corresponding to the 4 cm CT lesion. FDG-avid mediastinal lymph nodes at right paratracheal (4R), subcarinal (7) and left paratracheal (4L) stations. No avid hilar node on the left. No pleural effusion.
Abdomen/pelvis: Physiologic uptake in liver, bowel and urinary tract. Adrenals without abnormal uptake.
Bones: No abnormal osseous uptake.
reports.conclusion: Avid right lower lobe primary with ipsilateral and contralateral mediastinal nodal disease. No distant metastasis.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. No enhancing lesion. No acute infarct, hemorrhage or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Major flow voids preserved.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lower lobe, right bronchus or lung
conditions.note: adenocarcinoma, cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB

reports.text:
Specimens: A. Lymph node, station 4R. B. Lymph node, station 7. C. Lymph node, station 4L.
Gross: received fresh, multiple tan-pink fragments in each container.
Microscopic: All three stations show metastatic carcinoma forming glands, with tumor cells positive for TTF-1 and napsin A and negative for p40.
Ancillary: Tissue sent for molecular profiling and PD-L1; to follow as addendum.
reports.conclusion: Lymph nodes 4R, 7 and 4L: metastatic non-small cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, consistent with lung primary.

documents.title: Cervical mediastinoscopy
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - 03/19/2024
Preoperative diagnosis: right lower lobe lung mass with mediastinal adenopathy.
Postoperative diagnosis: same; frozen section positive for carcinoma.
Procedure: cervical mediastinoscopy with lymph node biopsy, stations 4R, 7 and 4L.
Anesthesia: general. EBL minimal. No complications.
Findings: Firm enlarged nodes at 4R, 7 and 4L, each sampled. Hemostasis confirmed.
Disposition: Same-day discharge to home with wife.
Clinical stage with PET and pathology: cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB, not a surgical candidate. Referred on to medical and radiation oncology.

Thoracic surgery

Seen in clinic 03/06/2024 for preoperative evaluation; consent and procedure planned at that visit.

documents.title: Check-in after biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Op note and path in. Called Mark. Neck incision healing, sore throat from the tube is gone. He's heard from the surgeon that it's adenocarcinoma in the nodes on both sides of the chest - stage 3, not an operation. Oncology appt April 15. He's planning to keep working until he knows the treatment schedule. Asked whether his smoking caused it - said that's the biggest risk factor, but quitting in 2017 was still the right thing and it helps now. Offered a visit anytime; he'd rather wait until he has the plan.

events.reason: new stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT, 04/15/2024

Diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of the right lower lobe, cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB, diagnosed by mediastinoscopy 03/19/2024. No treatment to date.

HPI: 60-year-old man seen with his wife. Persistent cough since about mid-January and a 10 kg unintentional weight loss over three months. Also follows with endocrinology and nephrology for diabetic kidney disease, and rheumatology for tophaceous gout. He saw a news story about a phase III trial comparing a new targeted drug with standard chemotherapy and wants to know if he should join.

PMH: type 2 diabetes with nephropathy and proliferative retinopathy (laser both eyes), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, tophaceous gout.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succinate 50, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, allopurinol 300. NKDA.
Social: 30 pack-years, quit 2017. No alcohol. Hotel maintenance engineer.
Family: maternal grandfather with lung cancer.

Exam: Appears cachectic. Decreased breath sounds at the right lower lobe. Heart regular. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. Abdomen benign. Remainder unremarkable.

Labs today: Hb 12.5, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. Fasting glucose 160. AST 35, ALT 30. Creatinine as resulted, eGFR reviewed for carboplatin dosing.
Imaging reviewed: CT 02/13 with 4 cm RLL mass and mediastinal adenopathy; PET-CT 02/26 without distant disease; brain MRI 03/05 negative.

Molecular (addendum 04/10): no EGFR, ALK, ROS1 or KRAS alteration detected. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 30%.

Assessment and plan:
Unresectable stage IIIB NSCLC. We talked through the trial he asked about in detail - what phase III means, randomization, and the potential benefits (access to a new drug, close monitoring) and risks (unknown side effects, possibly receiving the standard arm anyway). That study requires a specific targetable mutation, and his tumor has none, so he would not be eligible. The standard of care for him is concurrent chemoradiation with curative intent, followed by a year of durvalumab consolidation if there is no progression.
- Concurrent weekly carboplatin (AUC 2) and paclitaxel (45 mg/m2) with thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Radiation oncology consult arranged.
- Port not needed for weekly regimen; peripheral access.
He and his wife agree. Target start early May.

Thoracic oncology

documents.body: Treatment starts May 6, radiation every weekday for 6 weeks and chemo Mondays. HR at the hotel needs FMLA papers, intermittent at first. Oncology said their office or you could fill it out, they're backed up. Can you? Uploading the form.

documents.title: Check-in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came after radiation (session 12 of 30). Weekly chemo Mondays. Tired by afternoon but managing. Eating smaller meals more often. Working half days.
Sugars: fasting 140-170 at home. No lows. BP lower than usual, 130s at the cancer center.
Vitals as charted. Lungs: decreased at R base as before. Heart regular. No edema to speak of.
Oncology labs last week reviewed: Hb about 11, kidneys about the same.
A/P: Mostly here so we stay in the loop. No change to diabetes or BP meds during treatment - not chasing A1c right now. Flu/COVID in the fall are fine on immunotherapy. FMLA done. See after treatment.

documents.title: done with radiation
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last radiation was Friday, rang the bell. Wiped out but ok. Next step is the immunotherapy in July. Going back to work part time next week, HR has the papers you did.

documents.title: RE: done with radiation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations on getting through it. Rest when you need to. Let me know if anything with the sugars or BP feels off as you get back to normal eating.

documents.title: Chemoradiation treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY TREATMENT SUMMARY
Patient: Mark Desrosiers
Diagnosis: NSCLC, adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe, cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB
Intent: curative
Treatment: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the right lower lobe primary and involved mediastinal nodes, IMRT, 05/06/2024 - 06/14/2024. Completed without breaks.
Concurrent systemic therapy (medical oncology): weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 45 mg/m2, six cycles.
Tolerated treatment without unplanned breaks.
Plan: Restaging CT about 8-10 weeks after completion. Medical oncology to begin consolidation durvalumab if no progression.

Radiation oncology

medications.sig: 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for 12 months
medications.reason: consolidation after chemoradiation, stage IIIB NSCLC

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Thoracic oncology - 07/10/2024
Completed concurrent chemoradiation 06/14. Energy improving, weight stable. Cough less frequent. No fever, no new dyspnea.
Exam: lungs with decreased breath sounds at right base, unchanged; no rash.
Assessment: s/p chemoradiation for stage IIIB NSCLC; no clinical progression. Begin durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks, first dose today, planned 12 months. Immune-related adverse effects reviewed with him and his wife (lungs, bowels, skin, thyroid, liver, kidneys) and when to call. TSH and CMP with each cycle. Restaging CT early September.

Thoracic oncology

documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Retina follow-up 07/23/2024: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy OU, status post panretinal photocoagulation. Neovascularization regressed OU. No vitreous hemorrhage. OCT without macular edema. No further laser needed. Return in 12 months.

CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison 02/13/2024 and PET-CT 02/26/2024.
Right lower lobe mass decreased, now 2.1 cm. Mediastinal lymph nodes at 4R, 7 and 4L decreased in size. Post-radiation change in the right lower lobe and medial right lung, in the treatment field. No new pulmonary nodule. No pleural effusion. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Partial response of right lower lobe mass and mediastinal nodes after chemoradiation. Expected post-radiation change. No new disease.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY FOLLOW-UP - 10/14/2024

Interval: Seen here in January. Since then diagnosed with stage IIIB NSCLC, completed chemoradiation in June and now on durvalumab. Over the past few months, worsening fatigue and frothy urine. Diabetes poorly controlled, most recent A1c 9.2%. BP persistently high despite taking his medicines as prescribed.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, allopurinol 300 mg; durvalumab every 4 weeks via oncology. NKDA.

Exam: BP elevated (see vitals). Bilateral lower extremity edema. Lungs: decreased right base. Heart regular.

Labs 10/07/2024: creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (prior 1.4 last year), BUN 36 mg/dL, fasting glucose 198 mg/dL. UA 3+ protein. Urine albumin/creatinine 400 mg/g.

Assessment: CKD stage 3b, A3, from diabetic nephropathy with uncontrolled diabetes and hypertension.

Plan:
- Continue present medications.
- Sodium restriction under 2 g/day reviewed.
- Repeat labs and return in 6 months.

Outpatient nephrology
